video_title: How AI Is Turning Figma’s Finance Team Into Builders
gist: Figma's CFO describes a finance org where staff build their own AI tooling (Codex, ChatGPT agents, Figma Make) for collections, corp-dev diligence, T&E analysis and memo review, while core systems of record are still bought and a new CIO from Coinbase is tasked with centralizing bottoms-up tools. He says that if business complexity stayed flat Figma would need fewer finance people within a year, and a16z partners report that CFOs moved from AI-for-docs to AI-for-reconciliation in roughly the last nine months.

insights.claim: Figma's credit and collections lead rebuilt his entire workflow (invoice tracking, cash collections, reconciliation to NetSuite) as a homegrown AI-built system tied to Figma's other systems, freeing him to focus on driving down days receivable and to rebuild credit checks.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Mid-market AR/collections point solutions face substitution risk from in-house agent builds on top of the ERP.

insights.claim: Figma's corporate development team, staffed by finance people rather than product people, now uses 'can you vibe code the product' as a diligence check on acquisition targets to gauge how deep the technology moat is.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Acquirers are explicitly testing replicability with AI, which pressures valuations of thin-moat software targets.
insights.quote: can you vibe code a product is one of the one of the checks that we use in diligence now

insights.claim: Figma's corp-dev team built AI 'personalities' of each leader (e.g., the CFO, the CEO, the CRO) as skills to simulate an investment committee and pre-review M&A and investment memos, reducing the cycle time leaders spend together.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Simulated-reviewer agents are an emerging pattern for compressing executive decision cycles in document-heavy cultures.

insights.claim: Figma's finance team builds with a mix of tools: Codex for corp-dev work, ChatGPT agents and skills for credit and collections, and Figma's own Figma Make for prompt-built hosted apps, which also generates product feedback.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: OpenAI tools are embedded in a public-company finance org, and Figma is dogfooding Figma Make for internal business apps.

insights.claim: For 2027 planning, Figma's corporate finance team used AI to fuzzy-match T&E data across a travel tool (transcribed as "Non"), Zip and Ramp (e.g., distinguishing true off-site travel from local employees), producing visualized policy-change suggestions that the CFO said could not have been done by hand.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: The value is in cross-system data stitching on top of spend tools, a layer spend vendors may need to own or risk being commoditized.
insights.quote: 95% of the challenge there is just like getting your data in the right spot.

insights.claim: The Figma CFO accepts directionally correct AI output for exploratory analysis like T&E review, reserving 'picture perfect' rigor for outputs that require it.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Adoption is fastest where tolerance for error is high; audit-grade use cases lag.
insights.quote: I didn't need something 100% perfect. Um I just wanted something that was directionally, you know, in the right

insights.claim: A Figma self-serve go-to-market finance leader built Figma plugins to automate creation of recurring materials so the team spends time on annotation and discovery rather than reconciling last week's or month's numbers.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: FP&A time is shifting from reporting production to experiment and spend-allocation analysis.

insights.claim: Finance teams at Figma consistently appear in the company all-hands (Fig Nation) segment showcasing AI builds, and the CFO says he now uses access to AI tooling and visible internal building as a recruiting pitch.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: AI tool access is becoming a talent-competition lever, supporting enterprise seat expansion for AI vendors.
insights.quote: I don't know if folks are actually treating uh access technology as like a recruiting vehicle as much as they could or should.

themes.theme: Build vs buy and the CIO as productizer

insights.claim: Figma buys off-the-shelf solutions for core systems of record it cannot get wrong, while internal building is concentrated in workflow automation of low-thought tasks.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Systems-of-record vendors (ERP, billing) look more defensible than workflow-layer finance tools against in-house AI builds.
insights.quote: for like the core systems of record solutions and like the things that like we just can't mess up like yes we're going and buying solutions for that

insights.claim: The Figma CFO sees the evolved CIO function as taking bottoms-up tools built by specialists and productizing them into shared platforms that outlive their creators, e.g., one triage/follow-up platform for internal audit (SOX), GRC (ISO, SOC 2) and AP accruals.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Demand is emerging for internal-tool platforms and governance layers that consolidate sprawling employee-built agents.
insights.quote: the evolution of what a CIO function should or could be

insights.claim: Figma just hired Casper Sorenson from Coinbase as CIO, with a mandate to create centralized PM-type functions that partner with business teams and build foundations others build on.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Signals Figma is formalizing AI tool governance at the systems level.

insights.claim: The Figma CFO admits the company has grown faster than its supporting tooling and is in a 'messy middle' where some teams' AI builds are centralized and others ran ahead and now need help.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Even AI-forward public companies have fragmented internal tooling, a gap for orchestration and governance vendors.
insights.quote: I think we're in the messy middle right now.

insights.claim: An a16z growth-stage CFO reported their team created 40 to 50 agents in a month or two, and the a16z partner estimates perhaps 90% are no longer used, but argues the automation-first habit matters almost as much as the agents.
insights.speaker: Ivon Macarov (a16z)
insights.so_what: High agent churn means usage-based metrics on internal agent counts overstate durable adoption.

insights.claim: At one a16z growth-stage company, every customer success rep had vibe-coded a different dashboard showing different numbers, illustrating the need for a reconciling function over decentralized builders.
insights.speaker: a16z host
insights.so_what: Metric fragmentation from vibe coding creates demand for semantic layers and centralized definitions.

insights.claim: a16z sees a decentralized 'X engineer' pattern across functions (go-to-market engineer, talent engineer, finance engineer) staffed by finance people with engineering skills or borrowed product engineers, with no settled profile yet.
insights.speaker: a16z host
insights.so_what: New hybrid roles reshape who buys and builds enterprise software inside functions.

insights.claim: A hyper-growth a16z company said it must buy everything off the shelf because it is moving too fast to build.
insights.speaker: Ivon Macarov (a16z)
insights.so_what: Build-vs-buy splits by company stage and speed, keeping a market for vertical finance AI vendors.

insights.claim: Figma's CFO says that if business complexity stayed flat, Figma would probably not need the same number of finance people a year from now, but new products and acquisitions keep complexity outpacing efficiency gains.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: G&A headcount leverage at Figma (and peers) is likely, supporting operating margin expansion as complexity growth slows.
insights.quote: if our business complexity was like staying the same, I think we probably would wouldn't need the same number of people a year from now.

insights.claim: The Figma CFO wants to add finance headcount only when business complexity grows faster than automation can absorb, saying regular business-rhythm work can now move in the reverse direction.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Finance hiring decouples from revenue growth, a negative for seat-based finance software pricing.

insights.claim: Figma's CFO expects end-to-end automation to start with truly deterministic processes, but says getting audit-ready output for business-critical systems is a very high bar that depends on what makes auditors comfortable.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Auditor acceptance is the gating factor for fully autonomous close and accounting AI.

insights.claim: a16z partners report a step-function shift about nine months ago at their CFO and controller dinners, from using AI to generate tax memos or onboarding docs to automating core data reconciliation and workflows.
insights.speaker: a16z host
insights.so_what: Finance AI adoption has moved into core workflows, expanding the addressable market for reconciliation and close tools.

insights.claim: Finance leaders now feel compelled to adopt AI automation or be perceived as behind within their organizations, and finance teams are winning internal automation hackathons, which was not the case a couple of years ago.
insights.speaker: a16z host
insights.so_what: Social pressure is driving finance AI budget allocation regardless of measured ROI.

insights.claim: Boards and investors are receiving deeper analysis and faster iteration from finance teams, short-circuiting the old cycle of board questions followed by long rework.
insights.speaker: a16z host
insights.so_what: Board-reporting expectations are ratcheting up, raising the bar for portfolio-company finance teams.

insights.claim: a16z observes its CFO-tool investments shifting from tracking workflows to delivering the result (e.g., a completed reconciliation) with the audit trail as part of the product.
insights.speaker: a16z host
insights.so_what: Outcome-based finance software with built-in auditability is the product direction a16z is backing; workflow trackers face pressure.

insights.claim: The Figma CFO expects AI tools for accounting tasks like flux analysis of period-over-period GL changes to supply a first draft of what changed so accountants focus elsewhere, noting many such tools now exist.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Flux analysis and variance explanation are near-term wedges for accounting AI vendors.

insights.claim: AI lets teams consume multiple data sources and fuzzy-match a directionally correct reconciliation, replacing the old process where finance had to run SQL queries and act as its own BI analyst.
insights.speaker: Ivon Macarov (a16z)
insights.so_what: Reduces dependence on BI and data teams for finance analysis, pressuring traditional BI seats.

insights.claim: Excel is not under threat according to Figma's CFO, who calls it his 'love language' and the way he builds trust and intuition, comparing hands-on spreadsheet manipulation to using a color wheel versus prompting an agent in Figma.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Direct-manipulation interfaces stay sticky even as AI generates first drafts, favoring AI-in-the-spreadsheet over spreadsheet replacement.
insights.quote: Is Excel under threat? >> No. It's like my love language, dude.

insights.claim: An a16z partner says AI models are not yet good enough to create a forecast or financial model on their own, though the spatial organization of Excel remains valuable.
insights.speaker: a16z host
insights.so_what: AI-native FP&A modeling is still an open gap.
insights.quote: the models aren't quite good enough to like create a forecast or a model quite yet

insights.claim: The Figma CFO uses AI models to digest large team-built models (e.g., 20 tabs) to identify needle movers and the most sensitive assumptions.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Review and explanation of existing models is a concrete executive use case for spreadsheet-aware AI.

insights.claim: a16z's advice to companies starting finance automation is to begin with data integrity and tracking, ahead of closing books or board updates, because many early-stage companies track almost nothing.
insights.speaker: Ivon Macarov (a16z)
insights.so_what: Data foundation remains the prerequisite and bottleneck for finance AI ROI.
insights.quote: You start with the integrity of data.

insights.claim: New finance hires can now discover within weeks that a startup's revenue is calculated incorrectly for its business model, and a16z partners say they see more 'creative' early-stage ARR than ever before.
insights.speaker: Ivon Macarov (a16z)
insights.so_what: Early-stage ARR figures warrant extra diligence scrutiny.
insights.quote: More more creative uh ARR at the early stage uh than I've ever seen before.

insights.claim: Figma's finance team owns metric definitions and prioritizes consistency so that historical figures never change, which the CFO says builds credibility with the board and in earnings disclosures, even as AI makes redefining metrics easier.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Figma's management signals stable, consistent KPI disclosure as a priority.

insights.claim: Before AI, the Figma CFO wrote 400-500 line SQL queries mapping product usage data to Stripe financial data to create 'golden tables' fed via ETL into Salesforce and Marketo, which ended debates over what was true.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Usage-to-billing data joins were the original finance force multiplier, and AI now makes them accessible to non-technical staff.

insights.claim: The Figma CFO monitors hourly dashboards and daily metrics, arguing that catching anomalies early saves money while catching positive moves lets the company put more behind them.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Finance cadence has compressed from monthly/weekly to daily or intraday, raising demand for real-time data infrastructure.

insights.claim: In hiring a VP of Finance, the Figma CFO uses a sparse-information case study that tests whether candidates truly understand their AI-built model, its most sensitive drivers, and can communicate it, rather than just producing output.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Hiring signal is shifting from output production to model comprehension and judgment.
insights.quote: you don't want to outsource your thinking today

insights.claim: AI slop is now being called out in meetings, with one CFO saying AI produced so many docs that nothing could be found; Figma responded with internal policies requiring labeling of AI-written content.
insights.speaker: Ivon Macarov (a16z) / Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: Backlash against low-quality AI output creates demand for knowledge management, search and AI-content governance.
insights.quote: using AI just led to unlimited amount of docs that are being created every day

insights.claim: An a16z partner worries that relying on AI-native juniors could erode knowledge of what world-class work, such as a really good model, looks like.
insights.speaker: Ivon Macarov (a16z)
insights.so_what: Experienced finance talent may command a premium as a quality check on AI output.

insights.claim: A university professor told an a16z partner his course syllabus changed several times in one semester due to new model releases, so universities are reverting to fundamentals like analytical thinking and Excel rather than teaching AI.
insights.speaker: Ivon Macarov (a16z)
insights.so_what: The pace of model releases is outrunning formal education, shifting AI skilling onto employers.

insights.claim: The Figma CFO's advice for hiring a CFO is to find a business owner with operational rigor matching the CEO's, rather than a 'traffic cop', someone who can simplify the business model so everyone runs in the same direction.
insights.speaker: Pier Milwani (Figma CFO)
insights.so_what: The CFO role is being redefined toward operator and builder, with implications for finance software buyers.

insights.claim: a16z partners say equity storytelling with numbers, once mainly a pre-IPO concern, has moved to Series A and B fundraising, made easier by AI but also prone to overthinking.
insights.speaker: a16z host
insights.so_what: Early-stage companies need earlier finance sophistication, pulling forward finance hires and tooling.
